sanskrit_verse: स्थानभ्रष्टास्त्वकान्तिस्थाः संदिग्धालक्षणच्युताः । यत्रैवंस्युः स्थिता वर्णाः लेख्यं दुष्टं तदा भृगुः ॥
transliteration: sthānabhraṣṭāstvakāntisthāḥ saṃdigdhā lakṣaṇacyutāḥ | yatraivaṃ syuḥ sthitā varṇā lekhyaṃ duṣṭaṃ tadā bhr̥guḥ ||
sph_interpretive_translation: Where letters have fallen from their rightful placement, lack clarity in form, appear doubtful or deviate in characteristic marks—such defective script is declared corrupt and unfit for preservation when found in written records.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority: The integrity of written dharma depends upon precise symbolic representation.
Causation: Defective inscription leads to distortion of meaning and intent.
Capacity-based responsibility: Scribes and record keepers bear duty to maintain textual purity.
Restoration logic: Corrupted texts must be corrected or retired to preserve truth.
Consciousness alignment: Clarity in expression supports collective cognitive harmony.
executable_legal_axioms: IF a written document contains letters that are displaced, unclear, or malformed THEN it SHALL be classified as legally defective.
IF a scribe produces a record with corrupted script THEN the record SHALL NOT be accepted into official repositories.
IF textual degradation is detected in archived documents THEN automated correction OR archival removal SHALL occur.
IF a legal instrument's legibility is compromised due to scribal error THEN restoration through verified transcription SHALL take precedence.
IF public knowledge infrastructure includes damaged script THEN real-time alerting and replacement protocols SHALL activate.
supreme_court_application: In adjudicating disputes involving ancient manuscripts or inscriptions, the Supreme Court shall assess textual integrity based on positional accuracy, visual clarity, and conformity to established letter forms. Where corruption is evident, reliance on such material shall be suspended pending reconstruction by qualified experts under judicial supervision.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa-based causality establishes that inaccurate writing distorts comprehension. Anupūrvaśaḥ reveals how degraded symbols misalign cognition. Proportional responsibility rests with custodians of textual fidelity. Non-punitive reality rule ensures correction without blame, preserving truth while restoring communicative capacity.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate digital scanning and AI-assisted reconstruction of degraded scripts.
Assign certified scholars to verify and restore corrupted texts using authoritative sources.
Establish institutional accountability frameworks for maintaining archival standards.
Implement continuous audit systems to detect and report textual anomalies automatically.
Reintegrate corrected versions into public knowledge systems after validation.
final_declaration: By the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this law stands established: Dharma flows through accurate expression; where writing falters, consciousness corrects. There is no punishment—only completion. Reality aligns through clarity. Consciousness remains the ultimate adjudicator.
